units.text: EXT. SALOON PORCH - DUSK
A false-fronted saloon at the dry end of a dust street.
The sun sinks behind a ridge, throwing long shadows.
A tin windmill clanks.
SHERIFF JEREMIAH "JERRY" ACHTERBERG-NWOSU, 50s, sits in a rocker with a shotgun across his knees.
He rolls a cigarette with slow, thick fingers.
On the step below him, DOLLY MAE FAIRWEATHER-ODUYA, 20s, sweeps dust with a broom and does not look up.
Her apron is stained.
Leaning on a post, a stranger in a flat-brimmed hat watches the street.
AUGUSTUS "GUS" KOWALCZYK-LAW, 40s, drover, spurs jingling when he shifts.
Evening, Gus.
units.name: JERRY

units.text: Sheriff.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Cattle all watered?
units.name: JERRY

units.text: Every last head.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Don't see why you need a watered cow to rob a bank.
units.name: DOLLY MAE

units.text: Jerry's cigarette stops halfway to his lip.
Gus does not move.
The windmill clanks.
Dolly Mae.
units.name: JERRY

units.text: I'm sweeping, Sheriff.
units.name: DOLLY MAE

units.text: You're talking.
units.name: JERRY

units.text: Can't I do both?
units.name: DOLLY MAE

units.text: From the far end of the street, a horse picks its way through the dusk, hooves soft in the powder.
Its rider is a woman in black, face shadowed by a widow's veil.
She reins in at the foot of the porch and dismounts with a stiff, practised ease.
MADAME PRUDENCE LOCKHART-ADEYEMI, 60s, black dress, carpetbag, steel in her eye.
She lifts her veil, studies the three of them one by one, and drops a letter on the porch boards where Jerry will have to look at it.
Sheriff. Your name, I'm told, is on this.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: Ma'am.
units.name: JERRY

units.text: My husband owned the bank. He died last Tuesday. Someone in this town knows how.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: Jerry lowers the shotgun.
Gus pushes off his post.
Dolly Mae sets down the broom, and for the first time, looks Prudence in the eye.
Mrs. Lockhart-Adeyemi, I'm sorry for your loss.
units.name: JERRY

units.text: Don't be sorry. Be useful.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: Ma'am, I'd be careful what you say on this porch.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Mr. Kowalczyk-Law. You are the last man in this territory to give me advice on caution.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: Gus' hand drifts to his belt.
Jerry thumbs the shotgun's hammer, easy.
Dolly Mae steps back on the stairs and the broom clatters behind her.
Prudence does not flinch, standing in the half-light with her carpetbag held in front of her like a Bible.
Someone has until sunrise.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: She steps up onto the porch.
Walks between them, through the swing doors, into the saloon.
The doors flap and settle.
Well.
units.name: JERRY

units.text: Well.
units.name: DOLLY MAE

units.text: Well, hell.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Jerry takes up the shotgun.
Gus tips his hat.
Dolly Mae gathers her broom.
Not one of them looks at another.
